title: Open-immersion tensor piece
statement:
Let $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ be a chosen compactification [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification]. Work on the small pro-etale site $\mathcal C=\overline X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ in the chosen universe. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$, put $R_X=R|_X$, and identify $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with $\mathcal C/X$ [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization, def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Let $E\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_X))$ be arbitrary, and let $F^\bullet$ be a bounded complex of $R$-module sheaves whose terms are finite projective, meaning direct summands of finite free $R$-module sheaves as in [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Extension by zero $j_!$ and restriction $j^*$ are the exact module functors of [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], applied termwise to the unbounded derived categories. Use the derived tensor product of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Then the canonical open-immersion tensor map
$$
(j_!E)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}F^\bullet\longrightarrow j_!(E\otimes_{R_X}^{\mathbf L}Lj^*F^\bullet)
$$
is an isomorphism, natural in $E$ and $F^\bullet$. Here $Lj^*=j^*$; the displayed map is the inverse of the adjunction projection map $j_!(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}j^*F)\to j_!E\otimes^{\mathbf L}F$ (the transpose of the unit tensored with $j^*F$). This fixes its direction and normalization. Taking $R$ to be the coefficient ring sheaf on $\overline X$ gives the formula in the imported statement; no identification of different coefficient sheaves is assumed.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] (1) to replace $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ by $\mathcal C/X$; only the equivalence of underlying sites is used, not its constant-coefficient clause. On this localization [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] gives exact $j_!\dashv j^*$. By [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] these functors are computed termwise in the unbounded derived categories. Thus any complex $I$ representing $E$ can be used, $j_!I$ represents $j_!E$, and $j^*F$ represents $Lj^*F$. There is no boundedness condition on $I$.

source.place: Tag 09AE, definition-extension-zero; sites-modules.tex Tags 03DI/03DJ; derived.tex Tag 015F

proof.text: For an $R_X$-module $M$ and an $R$-module $P$, define $\alpha_{M,P}:j_!(M\otimes j^*P)\to j_!M\otimes P$ by adjunction from $\eta_M\otimes1:M\otimes j^*P\to j^*j_!M\otimes j^*P=j^*(j_!M\otimes P)$. The adjunction is [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], and the natural restriction-tensor identification is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor]. Hence $\alpha$ is natural in both variables. For $P=R^{\oplus N}$ it is the finite-sum identification $j_!(M^{\oplus N})\to(j_!M)^{\oplus N}$: on each inclusion the adjunct is the corresponding inclusion composed with $\eta_M$. This map is invertible: maps from $j_!(M^{\oplus N})$ to any $H$ correspond by adjunction to $N$ maps $M\to j^*H$, then to $N$ maps $j_!M\to H$; these are precisely the maps from $(j_!M)^{\oplus N}$. This verifies the coproduct universal property and identifies the comparison, including $N=0$.

source.place: Tags 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback); finite sums by the displayed adjunction

proof.text: Write $A(P)=j_!(M\otimes j^*P)$ and $B(P)=j_!M\otimes P$. For a package splitting $P\xrightarrow{i}R^{\oplus N}\xrightarrow{p}P$, $pi=1$, supplied by [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package], put $\beta_P=A(p)\alpha_{M,R^{\oplus N}}^{-1}B(i):B(P)\to A(P)$. Naturality of $\alpha$ gives $\beta_P\alpha_{M,P}=A(p)A(i)=1$ and $\alpha_{M,P}\beta_P=B(p)B(i)=1$. Consequently $\beta$ is independent of the splitting. For maps $u:M\to M'$ and $v:P\to P'$, invert the naturality equation for $\alpha$ to obtain $A(u,v)\beta_{M,P}=\beta_{M',P'}B(u,v)$. This gives naturality for arbitrary maps of finite-projective terms, even when the chosen splittings are not chain maps.

source.place: Proof, finite-projective term argument, expanded by finite-free retractions

proof.text: Each $F^r$ and $j^*F^r$ is flat: tensor with it is a retract of the exact functor $M\mapsto M^{\oplus N_r}$, using the package splitting; the splitting restricts to the localized site. Thus [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] makes $F$ and $j^*F$ K-flat. The derived tensor computation in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] then identifies $j_!E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}F$ with $\operatorname{Tot}(j_!I\otimes_R F)$ and $E\otimes_{R_X}^{\mathbf L}Lj^*F$ with $\operatorname{Tot}(I\otimes_{R_X}j^*F)$. Explicitly, to justify using the arbitrary representative $I$, choose K-flat resolutions of $I$ and $j_!I$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Tensoring either quasi-isomorphism with the indicated K-flat second factor remains a quasi-isomorphism: its cone is the tensor of the acyclic original cone, with the same cone signs, and is acyclic by [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Apply the canonical two-K-flat-factor identifications of the cited descent node. Exactness of $j_!$ preserves the resulting quasi-isomorphism on the source.

Apply the inverses $\beta_{I^a,F^r}$ of step 3 at each bidegree $(a,r)$. Under the total-complex definition [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], degree $n$ is the finite sum over $a+r=n$, since $F$ is bounded. The finite-sum identification of step 2 commutes $j_!$ with these sums. Naturality from step 3 gives $\beta_{I^{a+1},F^r}(j_!d_I\otimes1)=j_!(d_I\otimes1)\beta_{I^a,F^r}$ and $\beta_{I^a,F^{r+1}}(1\otimes d_F)=j_!(1\otimes j^*d_F)\beta_{I^a,F^r}$. Multiplying the second equality by $(-1)^a$ proves compatibility with $d_I\otimes1+(-1)^a1\otimes d_F$. Thus the finite sums of $\beta$ and $\alpha$ are inverse chain maps. Their image under localization is the displayed canonical map, because $\alpha$ was defined using precisely the unit and restriction-tensor comparison. For maps of representatives both variables' naturality equations hold termwise. These maps also descend to homotopy categories: a homotopy $h:I^a\to I'^{a-1}$ induces $j_!h\otimes1$ on the left total complex and $j_!(h\otimes1)$ on the right; a homotopy $k:F^r\to F'^{r-1}$ induces $(-1)^a1\otimes k$ in bidegree $(a,r)$ on either side, with restriction and $j_!$ where appropriate. In each case $dH+Hd$ is the difference of the induced chain maps, and naturality of $\beta$ with respect to $h$ or $k$ makes these homotopies commute with $\beta$. For quasi-isomorphisms the naturality equations remain true after inverting those maps, by step 4. This proves naturality in the derived object $E$ and in $F$, as well as the asserted isomorphism.
